track.legalName: Petition for Expungement or Resentencing of a Marijuana Conviction While Currently Serving (Mont. Code Ann. § 16-12-113(1)-(4), (8)-(12))
track.publicName: Marijuana conviction expungement or resentencing while serving a sentence
track.mechanism: Under § 16-12-113(1) a person CURRENTLY SERVING a sentence for an act that is permitted under Title 16, chapter 12, or that is punishable by a lesser sentence under that chapter than the person was awarded, may petition for expungement or resentencing. Section 16-12-113(2) directs the court to presume the petitioner satisfies the criteria unless the county attorney provides a reasonable basis otherwise, and, where the criteria are satisfied, to grant the petition UNLESS the court determines that granting it would pose an unreasonable risk of danger to public safety. That public-safety override does not appear in the subsection (6) pathway used by the completed-sentence track, and it is the principal reason the two are separate mechanisms rather than branches. Section 16-12-113(3) requires credit for time already served and prohibits supervision after resentencing; § 16-12-113(4) prohibits a term longer than the original sentence and prohibits reinstatement of charges dismissed under a negotiated plea agreement. Sections 16-12-114 through 16-12-116 define an expungement or resentencing of marijuana conviction court and authorise appointment of a decriminalized marijuana conviction expungement judge with the authority and power of an elected district court judge. Procedure is governed by the AF 22-0129 Temporary Rules and the Office of the Court Administrator publishes Form A specifically for the currently-serving posture, with the same Certificate of Service and Proposed Order.
exclusions: Acts that remain criminal at the same level under Title 16, chapter 12.
Convictions from out-of-state, federal or Tribal courts.
A participant who has completed the sentence, who belongs on the completed-sentence track under § 16-12-113(5).
Relief may still be refused where the court determines that granting the petition would pose an unreasonable risk of danger to public safety (§ 16-12-113(2)). That override is unique to this track.

units.label: MMRTA Form A petition in the sentencing court, with certificate of service and proposed order
units.description: The court stage, and the substantive heart of the track. MMRTA Form A is published by the Office of the Court Administrator specifically for the currently-serving posture: the caption, the 'I am currently serving my sentence for this conviction' recital and the resentencing election are all built into it. The adopted Batch 2 resolution memorandum controls here and is explicit that Form A is a packet product and that the currently-serving posture is a scope restriction and a substantive-choice warning rather than a reason to downgrade the mechanism to guidance. LegalEase completes the caption for the correct court level, the participant's identity and case facts, the offence selection the participant makes from the enumerated list, and the conviction date, and assembles the OCA Certificate of Service and the OCA Proposed Order. It does not choose between expungement and resentencing, does not calculate a resentencing result, and does not author any public-safety argument. Required attachments are the participant's DOJ criminal record and the supporting court documents.

units.label: Conditional DOJ CRISS submission, only where the court grants expungement
units.description: The conditional Department of Justice stage. Where the court grants EXPUNGEMENT the participant must separately submit the CRISS Expungement/Removal Request Form with the court judgment and the expungement order, because the court order does not itself clear the DOJ criminal history record. Where the outcome is RESENTENCING rather than expungement the conviction stands with a modified sentence, there is nothing for DOJ to delete, and this unit does not apply — the packet says so plainly rather than sending a request that will be refused. That conditionality is why the unit exists as a distinct unit rather than as a step inside unit 1.

track.venue: Whichever court sentenced the participant, on the same three caption options as the completed-sentence track. Sections 16-12-114 and 16-12-115 additionally define an expungement or resentencing of marijuana conviction court and permit appointment of a designated decriminalized marijuana conviction expungement judge; whether any such judge has been appointed, and whether that changes the practical filing destination in any county, is unresolved.

The offence-mapping question is a self-help boundary: whether the historical conduct is now permitted, or is now punishable by a lesser sentence, under Title 16, chapter 12 requires mapping decades-old charging language and quantities against the current chapter, and it is the central legal question of the track. LegalEase presents the enumerated statutory list and the participant selects; the free-text specify-offence path is an attorney handoff.

packetInstructions: YES — STAGED OFFICIAL-FORM PACKET. OCA MMRTA Form A is expressly designed for the currently-serving posture. That posture is a scope restriction and a substantive-choice warning, not a reason to downgrade the mechanism to guidance. LegalEase must not choose between expungement, misdemeanor resentencing, and civil-infraction resentencing or author a public-safety argument. After an expungement outcome, the participant must complete the separate DOJ CRISS stage.

Montana's three words are not interchangeable and participant copy must keep them apart. Expungement under § 46-18-1103(1) means to permanently destroy, delete or erase a record from the criminal history record information system maintained by the Department of Justice. What happens at the courts, law-enforcement agencies and prosecutors' offices is sealing, not destruction (§ 46-18-1110(2)(a)). Removal is the DOJ term for deleting a non-conviction record. Redesignation and resentencing are MMRTA outcomes and are neither.

The court order is not the end in Montana. Under § 46-18-1110(2)(b) the person whose records are being expunged, not the court and not the clerk, must send the order to the arresting agency, the prosecutor, the clerk and the Department of Justice, together with fingerprints and the DOJ form; § 46-18-204(2) holds the same pattern for deferred dismissals; and the OCA MMRTA instructions say the same. A Montana packet that stops at a signed court order leaves the conviction sitting on the participant's background check.

One complete form set per conviction, never a consolidated petition. The OCA instructions require a separate form for each conviction even where the convictions occurred at the same time. This is the opposite of the misdemeanour expungement track, where one petition covers the whole record, and the rules engine must not generalise across the two.

The OCA instructions state expressly that the participant must follow all applicable filing rules including local filing rules, and route the participant to the Court Locator for local rules and contact information. This is an acknowledged local-practice dependency and is built as a required lookup step.
participantQuestions: LegalEase does not choose among expungement, redesignation as a misdemeanour, and redesignation as a civil infraction. These are materially different outcomes with different consequences, the form requires the participant to choose, and the election is the participant's alone. Any analysis of which outcome is better is legal advice and triggers handoff.
scopeRestrictions: Approve ordinary route; current-sentence posture is a scope restriction; obtain companion OCA forms.
The public-safety override in § 16-12-113(2) is unique to this track and does not appear in the completed-sentence pathway. Any case where it is plausibly in play is a handoff.

The Misdemeanor Expungement in Montana packet (ER-100, ER-200 and the Statement of Inability to Pay Court Costs and Fees) and the Dismissal After Completing a Deferred Sentence packet (DS-100 and DS-200) are stamped '© 2025 Montana Legal Services Association and Montana Supreme Court Access to Justice Commission. This form may be used for non-commercial purposes only.' Expungement.ai is a paid product, so reproducing or distributing them inside a packet is a commercial use. They are drafting references only: never generated, never relabelled, never converted, never lightly rewritten, never runtime-selectable and never generation_allowed. The restriction changes source use, not the existence of the mechanism.

No participant-facing statement that the participant may deny the conviction after expungement, after a deferred dismissal, or after a non-conviction removal. No Montana perjury shield or restoration-to-prior-status provision was located in any of the three statutes, and whether a cleared record may lawfully be denied is a hard self-help stop.

releaseBlockers.question: Which CRISS Expungement/Removal Request Form version the Department of Justice enforces in practice, and what the current required attachment set is. The 2023 PDF and the 29 April 2024 DOCX disagree: the 2023 version requires valid photo identification for the Non-Conviction Removal and Deferred Imposition request types and requires the 'Original Court Order' for misdemeanour expungement, while the 2024 version drops the photo-ID requirement, requires the 'Original Court Judgement' instead, and adds 'Deferred Prosecution' to the fourth request type. Master Library Edition 1.1 retains the 2024 version as the supporting-process asset and does not retain the 2023 PDF. The 2024 version is used for legal design and the 2023 version is preserved as history only; the packet includes photo identification by default, which is the fail-closed reading, and asks for a certified copy of the judgment.

releaseBlockers.question: Master Library Edition 1.1 retains the CRISS Expungement/Removal Request Form as a SUPPORTING_PROCESS asset with document role SUPPORTING_FORM, not as a packet form. The authority gate treats a supporting-process asset as one that cannot back an official_pdf_fill component, so every Montana component that maps to it is recorded as an authority role mismatch. The classification is the issue, not the mechanism: the form is a genuine Department of Justice agency form, it carries no use restriction, § 46-18-1110(2)(b) and § 46-18-204(2) both refer to a form prepared by the department of justice, and it is the required and only vehicle for the DOJ stage of four Montana tracks and for the whole of the non-conviction removal track. The mapping is retained rather than dropped, because pointing at the retained asset is truthful and preserves traceability, and the asset-class question is carried here as an explicit release blocker and a proposed Edition 1.2 reclassification. Edition 1.1 is not modified.

releaseBlockers.question: Master Library Edition 1.1 gives the OCA MMRTA Proposed Order and the OCA MMRTA Certificate of Service the SAME document ID, MT-OCA-MMRTA, distinguished only by document role, ORDER against SERVICE. They are two different binaries with two different SHA-256 values, so a component that names MT-OCA-MMRTA matches two retained assets carrying conflicting hashes and the authority gate records an authority hash conflict. This is an Edition 1.1 source-identity problem rather than a defect in the Montana legal design: both forms exist, both are published by the Office of the Court Administrator, both are retained, and both are correctly placed in the packet. Each needs its own document ID in a successor edition before either component can be resolver-selectable. The mappings are retained and the tracks stay authority-gated.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: Montana's three words are not interchangeable and participant copy must keep them apart. Expungement under § 46-18-1103(1) means to permanently destroy, delete or erase a record from the criminal history record information system maintained by the Department of Justice. What happens at the courts, law-enforcement agencies and prosecutors' offices is sealing, not destruction (§ 46-18-1110(2)(a)). Removal is the DOJ term for deleting a non-conviction record. Redesignation and resentencing are MMRTA outcomes and are neither.

provenance.sourceStatement: Correct jurisdiction-specific terminology: "Expungement." Montana defines the word narrowly at § 46-18-1103(1): to permanently destroy, delete, or erase a record of an offense from the criminal history record information system maintained by the Department of Justice. What happens at the courts, law enforcement agencies, and prosecutors' offices is sealing, not destruction (§ 46-18-1110(2)(a)). Do not use the two words interchangeably in participant copy.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: The Misdemeanor Expungement in Montana packet (ER-100, ER-200 and the Statement of Inability to Pay Court Costs and Fees) and the Dismissal After Completing a Deferred Sentence packet (DS-100 and DS-200) are stamped '© 2025 Montana Legal Services Association and Montana Supreme Court Access to Justice Commission. This form may be used for non-commercial purposes only.' Expungement.ai is a paid product, so reproducing or distributing them inside a packet is a commercial use. They are drafting references only: never generated, never relabelled, never converted, never lightly rewritten, never runtime-selectable and never generation_allowed. The restriction changes source use, not the existence of the mechanism.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: The court order is not the end in Montana. Under § 46-18-1110(2)(b) the person whose records are being expunged, not the court and not the clerk, must send the order to the arresting agency, the prosecutor, the clerk and the Department of Justice, together with fingerprints and the DOJ form; § 46-18-204(2) holds the same pattern for deferred dismissals; and the OCA MMRTA instructions say the same. A Montana packet that stops at a signed court order leaves the conviction sitting on the participant's background check.
